gloss: manual labor at a temple; cleaning and maintenance work (in Zen Buddhism)

definitions.gloss: manual labor at a temple; cleaning and maintenance work (in Zen Buddhism)
definitions.explanation: Originally a Zen Buddhist term for daily physical work considered part of spiritual practice.

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}の{作務|さむ}で{庭|にわ}を{掃|は}いた。
examples.english: I swept the garden during the morning work session.

examples.japanese: {作務衣|さむえ}を{着|き}て{作務|さむ}に{取|と}りかかる。
examples.english: I put on work clothes and start the temple chores.

examples.japanese: {禅寺|ぜんでら}では{作務|さむ}も{修行|しゅぎょう}の{一環|いっかん}とされる。
examples.english: At Zen temples, manual labor is considered part of spiritual training.

notes:
A Zen Buddhist concept where daily physical labor — sweeping, cleaning, cooking, gardening — is regarded as a form of meditative practice equal in value to seated meditation ({座禅|ざぜん}). The word is best known through the compound {作務衣|さむえ}, the simple work clothing worn during these tasks.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {作務衣|さむえ}: work clothes (originally for temple work, now popular as casual wear)
- {作務|さむ}をする: to do temple work
- {朝|あさ}の{作務|さむ}: morning work session

CULTURAL NOTE:
{作務衣|さむえ} has become popular as comfortable casual clothing beyond temple settings. Many craftspeople, artists, and restaurants use {作務衣|さむえ} as work uniforms.

RELATED WORDS:
- {修行|しゅぎょう}: ascetic training, spiritual discipline — broader term for religious practice
- {座禅|ざぜん}: seated meditation — the contemplative counterpart to active {作務|さむ}
